content.page_summary: Guidance on classification of pulmonary embolism (PE) severity and risk of early (in-hospital or 30 day) death, including a table (Table 8) mapping haemodynamic instability, clinical severity parameters (PESI/sPESI), RV dysfunction on imaging (TTE or CTPA), and elevated cardiac troponin levels to risk categories (high, intermediate-high, intermediate-low, low). Notes specify that testing for laboratory biomarkers such as cardiac troponins or natriuretic peptides is not necessary for immediate therapeutic decisions in high-risk PE and reference prognostically relevant imaging cut-offs presented elsewhere.
content.table_title: Classification of pulmonary embolism severity and the risk of early (in-hospital or 30 day) death (Table 8)
key_points: High-risk PE defined by haemodynamic instability (cardiac arrest, obstructive shock: systolic BP <90 mmHg or need for vasopressors to maintain BP ≥90 mmHg with end-organ hypoperfusion; or persistent hypotension: systolic BP <90 mmHg or drop ≥40 mmHg for >15 min not due to arrhythmia, hypovolaemia, or sepsis).
Intermediate risk subdivided into intermediate-high and intermediate-low based on combinations of clinical parameters, imaging (RV dysfunction on TTE or CTPA), and elevated cardiac troponin levels.
Low risk characterized by absence of the listed indicators; assessment of some parameters optional and, if assessed, should be negative.
imaging_and_tests: PESI = Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index; sPESI = simplified PESI
references_and_figures: Refers to section 7 and Figure 6 for reperfusion treatment decision pathway
Mentions Supplementary Data Figure 1 and Supplementary Data Table 3 for prognostic imaging cut-offs
Table 4 referenced for clinical presentations defining haemodynamic instability

thresholds_and_definitions_from_text.obstructive_shock_or_cardiac_arrest: systolic BP <90 mmHg or vasopressors required to achieve BP ≥90 mmHg in combination with end-organ hypoperfusion
thresholds_and_definitions_from_text.persistent_hypotension: systolic BP <90 mmHg or a systolic BP drop ≥40 mmHg for >15 min not caused by new-onset arrhythmia, hypovolaemia, or sepsis
